title: The dead boss lies as a tentacle carcass the seat's guns take apart in stages: segments of hit points, limbs severed, the core cracked, SCORCHED
context: Owner, 2026-10-10: "after the boss is dead, the user should still be able to shoot at its carcass, what would it take to create 'stages of destruction' for the dead boss? limbs getting cut, parts disappearing in explosion, etc." He chose option A: reuse the Reed carcass system (2026-10-10-boss-bait-carcass-tentacles), scaled up, with a severing rule and multi-hit stages, and a cross-fade from the boss's skin into the carcass. Before this, KILLED stopped the seat's guns (a held trigger fired nothing) and the boss lay as its frozen v1 collapse until R. The kit (src/fx/nih-dairia/*), src/sentry-pilot.js and the game's src/fx/* are untouched.
outcome: THE CONVERSION (src/labs/boss/remains.js, bait mode only): 1.5 s (`bossCarcass.settle`) after KILLED the boss's carcass is built as a Reed's (src/labs/boss/carcass.js `build`, now exported) from its own rest nodes by the kit's limb rule: 6 limbs of 10 rings, a tube of 10 sides in 13 pieces a limb (thin 0.8, the Reed's 0.6), a core ellipsoid of 1.05 the torso's spread, the cracked core's chunks built in and hidden: 6,380 triangles. It lies in a group of its own, a copy of the rig's frame at that moment. The solver stops then (no update, no re-anchor while it lies); the skin's material switches to alphaHash and its opacity falls 1 to 0 over 0.8 s while the carcass's rises 0 to 1 (a dithered dissolve both ways), then the skin is hidden. The carcass's colour is the skin's mean tissue colour (tissueOf is now cached per variant). The kernel is kept: R's newRound clears the carcass, gives the skin its material back and resets the same body. NO TIME DECAY: it lies until R; only fire takes it apart; its thermal warmth cools over 120 s (squared). THE FIRE: the seat's guns stay live after KILLED while the carcass lies (game-seat `afterKill`); after KILLED a round goes to the carcasses only (the Reeds' and the boss's), not to the fight. `carcassDamage`: the 40 mm 1 hit point to every target within 3 m, the 25 mm 0.2 to at most 3 within 2 m, the MK-9 destroys its 55 m ring; `blastBreaks` takes a `reach` per target (the core is metres wide). Each segment has 3 hp, the core 8, each chunk 3; a hurt target darkens toward char (a vertex colour written only when hurt, 0.85 at its last hit point). A segment at 0 is flung off as a Reed's piece; one broken on the body that is not a tip cuts off every segment beyond it on its limb (`severance`, runs between breaks each its own piece): the piece hops ~8 m away from the cut over 1.1 s (`hopOf`/`hopPose`: out fast and slowing, 3 m up, turned about up, rocked and level again), its vertices baked where it lands, still a target, and crumbles tip first over 90 s (`severedCrumble`). The core at 0 cracks: it goes and 3-5 chunks (`coreChunks`, seeded; jagged flat-shaded icosahedra, scorched) hop out onto the ground and lie, 3 hp each. THE STAGE (`carcassStage`, never going back): INTACT, LIMBS SEVERED n/6 (limbs cut by fire), CORE CRACKED, SCORCHED (nothing left on the body: no attached segment, no core, no chunk); the round's bar row shows it after the hits (round.js `remains`, .rd-stage). COST: nothing a frame at rest but the fade and the warmth (0.0-0.1 ms in the readout's carcass line); vertices are rewritten only for pieces flying, crumbling or hopping, the index only when a piece comes or goes. The handle has killBoss(), remains() and closeToBoss(back, up, at).
alternatives: Freeing the boss's kernel at the conversion (rejected: R's restart resets the same creature; freeing it would need a rebuild through the kit's factory, a load hitch on every restart)
A time decay for the boss's carcass as the Reeds' (rejected: the owner wants to take it apart; only fire destroys it, and it lies until R)
Fading the skin with transparent blending (rejected: sorting with the transmissive skin; alphaHash dithers with depth writes kept)
The fight's 40 mm damage radius (22 m) for the carcass (rejected: one landing would hit a whole limb and the core at once; 3 m reads a limb cut where it is hit)
Splitting a severed piece again when one of its middle segments breaks (deferred: the segment goes, the rest of the piece stays as one)
evidence: node --check on every edited file; npm test (230 programs; test/boss-carcass-stages.mjs new: the content, the boss's 6 limbs of 10 rings read from its asset, each gun's harm and the reach, severance runs, the hop out and level, 3-5 chunks seeded, the severed crumble tip first, the char, the stage machine never back, a six-limb carcass played by the rules: two 40 mm landings break nothing, the third cuts the limb to its tip, the MK-9 on the core cracks it, more fire to SCORCHED), npm run check, npm run build green

from a snapshot, sequentially, one headless Chrome (memory WARN on pinned swap, ~31 % headroom): --boss-carcass new and green: the carcass laid 1.50 s after the kill, the skin and the carcass cross-fading over ~0.6 s of lab clock and the skin hidden, 6 limbs of 13 pieces and 4 hidden chunks, 6,380 triangles, the solver stopped, INTACT; the 40 mm on limb 0's middle: nothing broke before the 9th landing that hurt it (the rounds scatter along the limb), then the limb cut at segment 1 and its 11 outer segments hopped 7.2-10.7 m and lay severed, LIMBS SEVERED 1/6; a severed piece still a target; the MK-9 on the core broke 77 targets and cracked it into 4 chunks lying 6.6-7.9 m out, CORE CRACKED; the 40 mm on what stood to SCORCHED (0 standing); R: the skin whole (opacity 1, no alphaHash), the solver stepping, no stage

--boss-friends and --boss green; --boss-bait green on its second run (its first failed before the kill, on Isao's gap median 16.2 m against 17-23, code this change does not reach), its held trigger after KILLED now firing nothing during the collapse and again on the carcass; --boss-wave red at its Reed-carcass 40 mm check ('a 40 mm round landed on the carcass': no 40 mm blast recorded on carcass 0 in 40 s while it crumbled by time), and red the same way on HEAD a0529f83 from a git-archive snapshot: a failure that predates this change, open
